newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX soars to second successive high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX soars to second successive high.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange closed at a second successive high and in heavy volumes on Wednesday, benefiting from a rally on Wall Street on Tuesday and from orders brought forward ahead of a long weekend.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 5,985.17 points, up 32.25. Traders said rallying chemicals TVK played a key role in driving the BUX higher.
Volumes were unusually heavy in oil company MOL, TVK and pharmaceuticals Richter, with over 755,000 shares, 593,000 shares and 239,000 shares traded, respectively.

"The Budapest bourse will be closed on Thursday and Friday, while London will be closed on Monday, therefore many investors might have brought forward their purchases," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities.
"Of course, the Dow's rally contributed, too."
Analysts said the Hungarian market was now in focus of investors' attention with earnings reports and international placements coming.

"Clearly first quarter results are driving earnings momentum, basically demonstrating that earnings momentum is there," said Tom Chadwick, Vice President for emerging European markets at Merrill Lynch in London.
"I think we're going to get a raft of strong first quarter results coming out in the next few days and I think the market begins to realise that the Hungarian equities are not losing their momentum."
Share offers in MOL, Richter and tile maker Zalakeramia are going to take place.
On Wednesday, TVK and Richter surged to new record levels of 3,005 forints and 14,250 forints, although both closed below the new peaks.
Traders said earlier today that TVK benefited from expectations of very strong first quarter earnings, while Richter continued to rise on its January-March profit report.
Elsewhere on the market, chemicals Borsodchem was also a strong gainer, it closed at the day's peak of 6,650 forints, up 150, rising on its CEO's comments.
Laszlo F. Kovacs told Reuters this morning that Borsodchem has fulfilled legal requirements for a corporate tax break.
Inter-Europa Bank gave up 1,950 forints to finish at 47,000, amid speculations about its planned bonus share issue.
